hints: At constant speed on a horizontal road, the driving force balances the 850 N resistance.
Use the instantaneous power relation $P = F_D \times v$ with $v = 42\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Multiply $850 \times 42$ to obtain the power in watts, and divide by 1000 to convert to kilowatts (kW).
walkthrough:
Since the car moves on a horizontal road at constant speed, acceleration is zero, meaning the engine driving force balances the resistance force:
$$F_D = 850\text{ N}$$

Calculate the power developed by the engine using $P = F_D \times v$ with $v = 42\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 850 \times 42 = 35700\text{ W}$$

Convert the power to kilowatts:
$$P = \frac{35700}{1000} = 35.7\text{ kW}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the formula for power developed by a driving force at velocity $v$:
$$P = F_D \times v$$

Because the car travels at constant speed on horizontal ground, Newton's first law tells us the forward driving force equals the resistance force:
$$F_D = F_{\text{res}} = 850\text{ N}$$

Substitute $F_D = 850\text{ N}$ and $v = 42\text{ m s}^{-1}$ into the power formula:
$$P = 850 \times 42$$

Divide by $1000$ to express the final answer in kilowatts as requested:
$$P = \frac{35700}{1000} = 35.7\text{ kW}$$

hints: The power increases by $6\text{ kW} = 6000\text{ W}$, giving a new total power of $P_{\text{new}} = 35700 + 6000 = 41700\text{ W}$.
At the instant the power is increased, the car's speed is still $v = 42\text{ m s}^{-1}$; calculate the new driving force: $F_{\text{new}} = \frac{P_{\text{new}}}{v} = \frac{41700}{42}$.
Apply Newton's second law horizontally: $F_{\text{new}} - F_{\text{res}} = ma \implies \frac{41700}{42} - 850 = 1200a$.
Solve for $a$ in exact fraction form $\frac{5}{42}\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and round to 3 significant figures ($0.119\text{ m s}^{-2}$).
walkthrough:
Calculate the new power developed by the engine:
$$P_{\text{new}} = 35.7 + 6 = 41.7\text{ kW} = 41700\text{ W}$$

Calculate the instantaneous new driving force at the current speed $v = 42\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{P_{\text{new}}}{v} = \frac{41700}{42} = \frac{6950}{7} \approx 992.857\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law $F_{\text{net}} = ma$ horizontally to the car of mass $m = 1200\text{ kg}$ against the $850\text{ N}$ resistance:
$$F_D - 850 = 1200a \implies \frac{41700}{42} - 850 = 1200a$$
$$\frac{41700 - 35700}{42} = 1200a \implies \frac{6000}{42} = 1200a$$

Solve for the instantaneous acceleration $a$:
$$a = \frac{6000}{42 \times 1200} = \frac{5}{42} \approx 0.119048\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 0.119\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Calculate the increased power of the engine in watts:
$$P_{\text{new}} = 35700 + 6000 = 41700\text{ W}$$

Determine the new forward driving force $F_D$ at the instant when velocity is still $v = 42\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{P_{\text{new}}}{v} = \frac{41700}{42}\text{ N}$$

State Newton's second law for the horizontal motion of the car:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma \implies F_D - F_{\text{res}} = ma$$

Substitute $F_D = \frac{41700}{42}\text{ N}$, $F_{\text{res}} = 850\text{ N}$, and mass $m = 1200\text{ kg}$:
$$\frac{41700}{42} - 850 = 1200a$$

Express $850$ as a fraction with denominator $42$:
$$850 = \frac{850 \times 42}{42} = \frac{35700}{42}$$
$$\frac{41700 - 35700}{42} = 1200a \implies \frac{6000}{42} = 1200a$$

Divide both sides by $1200$ to find acceleration $a$:
$$a = \frac{6000}{42 \times 1200} = \frac{5}{42}\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Convert $\frac{5}{42}$ to a decimal rounded to 3 significant figures:
$$a = \frac{5}{42} \approx 0.119048\text{ m s}^{-2} = 0.119\text{ m s}^{-2} \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$

hints: Connect engine power, forward driving force, and speed using $P = F_D \times v$, converting $80\text{ kW}$ to $80000\text{ W}$ at speed $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
At constant speed up the incline, acceleration is zero, so the forward driving force balances all opposing forces along the slope.
Identify the two opposing forces acting down the hill: resistance ($850\text{ N}$) and the downslope component of weight ($mg\sin\theta = 1200 \times 10 \times \sin\theta = 12000\sin\theta$).
Set up $F_D = 850 + 12000\sin\theta$, substitute $F_D = \frac{80000}{24}$, and solve for $\theta$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the engine driving force $F_D$ moving up the hill at constant speed $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with power $P = 80\text{ kW} = 80000\text{ W}$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{80000}{24} = \frac{10000}{3} \approx 3333.33\text{ N}$$

Since the car travels up the hill at constant speed, acceleration is zero, so the driving force balances both the resistance and the downslope component of weight:
$$F_D - 850 - mg\sin\theta = 0 \implies \frac{10000}{3} - 850 - 12000\sin\theta = 0$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the relationship connecting power, driving force, and velocity:
$$P = F_D \times v \implies F_D = \frac{P}{v}$$

Convert power $P = 80\text{ kW}$ to watts and substitute velocity $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{80000}{24} = \frac{10000}{3}\text{ N}$$

Analyze the forces acting parallel to the hill. Because the speed is constant, the net force along the slope is zero ($a = 0$):
$$F_D - F_{\text{res}} - mg\sin\theta = 0$$

Substitute the mass $m = 1200\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and resistance $F_{\text{res}} = 850\text{ N}$:
$$\frac{10000}{3} - 850 - 1200(10)\sin\theta = 0$$
$$\frac{10000}{3} - 850 - 12000\sin\theta = 0$$

Subtract $850$ from $\frac{10000}{3}$ by placing over a common denominator:
$$\frac{10000}{3} - \frac{2550}{3} = \frac{7450}{3}$$
$$\frac{7450}{3} = 12000\sin\theta$$

Divide both sides by $12000$ to isolate $\sin\theta$:
$$\sin\theta = \frac{7450}{3 \times 12000} = \frac{7450}{36000} = \frac{149}{720} \approx 0.206944$$

Take the inverse sine to find the angle $\theta$:
$$\theta = \arcsin\left(\frac{149}{720}\right) \approx 11.944^\circ = 11.9^\circ \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$
